summary: Randolph County, WV Forest Service tower built 1930 near Spruce Knob; now gone, with 2008 footing photos and a Forest Service group campground on the site.

facts.status_note: Weebly lists the tower as removed and FFLOS lists the site as ground with the tower gone; the latest photos show footings only

access.note: Site is now a developed Forest Service campground (Gatewood Group Campground), listed for 2026 with an April 16 opening; the tower itself is gone

events.note: Register 'Built' field gives 1930; Weebly, citing a Forest Service history, gives the same year and a construction cost of $1,495.05
Register page carries a 1933 photo credited to the National Archives
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg
Two photos of footings captioned October 2008, courtesy of Andy FitzGibbon

evidence.supports: tower was in what is now the Gatewood Group Camping Area, several miles from Spruce Knob, the state's high point
evidence.quote: This tower was located in what is now Monongahela National Forest's Gatewood Group Camping Area, several miles down the road from the state's high point at Spruce Knob.

evidence.supports: register lists the tower as built in 1930
tower constructed in 1930 on the Potomac Ranger District at a cost of $1,495.05
evidence.quote: 1930: Gatewood Fire Tower on the Potomac Ranger District was constructed at a cost of $1,495.05.

evidence.supports: the 1930 cost is credited to a Forest Service history
evidence.quote: Monongahela National Forest 1915 - 1990, USDA Forest Service

evidence.supports: a 1933 photograph credited to the National Archives
two photographs of footings captioned October 2008
evidence.quote: Footings in October 2008 - courtesy of Andy FitzGibbon

evidence.supports: the tower is listed as removed
the site is listed as ground, tower gone
evidence.quote: Gatewood Randolph 38.71781 -79.58389 Ground Gone FFLOS US 158, WV 8

evidence.supports: staffing for the towers was being phased out by the 1970s
evidence.quote: By the 1970s staffing for fire towers was being phased out.
Most towers were just torn down.

evidence.supports: one article names Red Oak and Olson as the surviving towers
evidence.quote: only two, Red Oak and Olson towers, remain intact at their original locations

evidence.supports: another article names Red Oak, Bickle and Olson as surviving
evidence.quote: only three, Red Oak, Bickle , and Olson , remain accessible in their original locations

evidence.supports: the spot is now a small Forest Service group campground on a ridge at a former fire tower site
evidence.quote: Gatewood Campground is a small group campground located on a ridge at a former fire tower site.

evidence.supports: the campground is at the end of Forest Road 131, about two miles east of Spruce Knob Lake Campground
evidence.quote: Gatewood is approximately two miles east of Spruce Knob Lake Campground at the end of Forest Road 131.

evidence.supports: Gatewood Group Campground has an April 16 opening for 2026
the Forest Service lists the site among developed recreation sites for 2026
evidence.quote: The 2026 opening dates for developed recreation sites are now available.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Potomac district page calls the site Gatewood Campground; the 2026 opening list calls it Gatewood Group Campground. Both point to the campground on the former tower site.
wvforestry.com names Red Oak and Olson as the two surviving towers; monforesttowns.org names Red Oak, Bickle and Olson. Gatewood is on neither list, so the story reports both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Removal year is not in any source, so no removed event is recorded. Public status is inferred from the Forest Service listing of the campground as a developed recreation site; check seasonal access before any visit. The 1933 photo caption does not say it shows the tower itself. The brief's access 'unknown' can be updated to public. Sources differ on which towers survive (Bickle); this story does not depend on it.
